title: 49ers-Seahawks: Mike Evans trolls Trevon Diggs in viral confrontation - CBS Sports
description: Evans explained that he asked, "Who are you?" before checking Diggs' jersey and realizing who was talking trash t
body:
Evans explained that he asked, "Who are you?" before checking Diggs' jersey and realizing who was talking trash to him
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:42 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The rivalry between the San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks heated up during their Week 5 matchup, and in one instance of the tensions bubbling to the surface, 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans took his trash-talking with Seahawks cornerback Trevon Diggs to a disrespectful, albeit hilarious, level.The two exchanged words at the end of a play, and Evans turned around, grabbed Diggs by the shoulders and twisted him so he could see the name on the back of his jersey. The name-check could be perceived as a show of dismissal, but Evans said after the game that he was legitimately curious who was talking to him."I was blocking him until the whistle," Evans said. "He said something like I'm doing extra, or something like that. I didn't know that was him at first. I played against him a few times, and we've always been cool. He was a good player. I honestly didn't know it was him, because in the helmet, it's hard to tell sometimes. We were talking trash, and I think I pushed him. I was like, 'Who are you?' I looked to make sure. I was like, 'Oh, it's f---ing Diggs.' Then he pushed me. Should've been a penalty."
Evans would remember Diggs from the three games they played against each other with their previous teams. Evans and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers defeated Diggs and the Dallas Cowboys in the 2021 and 2022 regular seasons before the roles reversed in an NFC Wild Card game in January 2023.
Diggs made a massive name for himself during the peak of his career when he led the NFL in interceptions, earned a first-team All-Pro selection and secured the first of two Pro Bowl nods in 2021. He followed that campaign up with another standout season in 2022 and garnered a massive five-year, $97 million contract extension with the Cowboys.In the years since, however, Diggs battled injuries and bounced from the Cowboys to the Green Bay Packers and eventually to the Seahawks. Seattle elevated Diggs from its practice squad for Sunday's game.Name-checking a player who was recently among the league's best defensive players and is now battling for a roster spot is the kind of troll work that goes viral on social media. Evans made waves throughout the NFL community for his trash-talking theatrics.
"Mike plays with an edge," 49ers offensive tackle Trent Williams said to CBS Sports Bay Area. "He plays with a huge edge. Something that you wouldn't expect a receiver to have. But that was pretty funny."

title: Commanders minority owner Magic Johnson reacts to clock-management blunder vs. Giants - CBS Sports
description: Johnson joined Commanders fans in questioning a disastrous
body:
Johnson joined Commanders fans in questioning a disastrous final sequence that cost Washington an opportunity to defeat the Giants
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:45 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        The Commanders' complete meltdown at the end of overtime, with the clock running out before a possible game-winning field goal attempt, left everyone stunned. Giants players jumped for joy as the clock expired on the 27-27 tie. Commanders players hunched over in disbelief. Dan Quinn threw his headset to the ground in disgust. Even FOX announcers Chris Myers and Jonathan Vilma were a mix of disbelief, confusion and shock.As for Commanders minority owner Magic Johnson? Well, he's just like us.
Here's the play in question, by the way:
Johnson is absolutely correct in that Washington simply had to kick a short field goal to win and that there was no need for the clock to come into play at all. Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels took blame, but this was a complete failure by all involved, and Quinn took the blame many times."After the first down run, still trying to gain more for the kick. Right call is honestly we can go clock it early and don't put ourselves in that spot, and that's my responsibility, nobody else's."Johnson became a part-owner of the organization in 2023 when Josh Harris bought the franchise from Daniel Snyder.
Washington is 1-3-1 this season and 3-13-1 over its last 17 games dating back to last season.

description: Drake Maye bounced back, Kyler Murray found his rhythm and Ashton Jeanty struggled on the ground as we sort throu
body:
Drake Maye bounced back, Kyler Murray found his rhythm and Ashton Jeanty struggled on the ground as we sort through key buy-low and sell-high trade targets across the league
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:59 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Week 5 was a wild one for Fantasy Football action. Let's take a look at some of the key takeaways, winners, losers, buy low and sell high candidates as we move forward. Jacksonville 19 – Philadelphia 17WINNER: Jalen Hurts, QB, EaglesAn encouraging game for him, even if the numbers don't show it. The 40 pass attempts really stand out. Could the Eagles start throwing more, even when Saquon Barkley returns? The schedule is about to be GREAT for Hurts. I'm not saying buy low because the Eagles offense has some warts, but this was a step in the right direction.Green Bay 31 – Chicago 7WINNER, I GUESS?: Marshawn Lloyd, RB, PackersMaybe Josh Jacobs returns soon, but as long as he remains out, Marshawn Lloyd is the best option in the Packers backfield. He averaged 3.1 yards per carry against a bad Bears run defense, so I'm not getting too excited. All of Kaleb Johnson's carries were in garbage time.FLUSH IT AND FORGET IT: The Bears offenseCaleb Williams could return next week and they will start rocking and rolling again.
New York Giants 27 – Washington 27SELL HIGH: Jacory Croskey-Merritt, RB, CommandersHe had a great game, which included a 33-yard TD run on the opening possession. It's certainly possible that Jayden Daniels opens this offense up for him, but the Giants are a great matchup. The schedule is about to get much tougher. He rarely catches a pass. I say "sell high (if you can)" because I'm not sure anyone is buying.WINNER: Anyone with NFL clock management experience. The Commanders are hiring.New England 45 – Las Vegas 17WINNER: Drake Maye, QB, PatriotsHe's back. I'm an idiot for doubting him.LOSER: MeI doubted Drake MayeNOT SURE HOW I FEEL ABOUT HIM: Ashton Jeanty, RB, Raiders10 carries for 27 yards, but of course, six targets and 50 receiving yards. He has not been efficient as a rusher. I bet his managers are panicking. He also came into the game nicked up. I might want to buy low. Listen to the Fantasy Football Today Podcast this week to find out!Pittsburgh 34 – Indianapolis 22LOSER: Josh Downs, WR, ColtsCan't trust him. He's a WR3. Downs will have good games in the future, but they will be hard to predict. Also, Keenan Allen had more targets. Not cool!
WINNER: Jaylen Warren, RB, SteelersThis guy is awesome. The Steelers always want to use two RBs, and Jaylen Warren is always the better guy. Rico Dowlde could be back next week, but Warren should be featured. I suppose I'd trade him for Ashton Jeanty, since I think Dowdle will have something of an annoying role, but if you have Warren on your team, I think you're going to be happy.Cincinnati 31 – Miami 24LOSER: Chase Brown, RB, BengalsWe might have a problem here. He fumbled, and Samaje Perine started getting more work. The Bengals are going into their bye and I fully expect Chase Brown to be their lead back after the bye, but the lack of rushing yards and lack of overall production is concerning. Remember, he had 11 catches last week with Ja'Marr Chase injured.WINNER: Ollie Gordon, RB, DolphinsI must say, I'm surprised and impressed. Two good-to-great games in a row for Gordon. I do think he's a clear winner and someone you can trust as a flex, but you can also try to sell high. Two catches but for zero yards in these two games. Shoot for the stars
Houston 26 – Tennessee 3WINNER: CJ Stroud, QB, TexansStroud has scored at least 20.5 points (6 point per passing TD leagues) in every game with Nico Collins. He's worth using in good matchupsLOSER: Carnell Tate, WR, TitansJust when you thought you could trust him! The Texans were allowing the most points to WRs, but I'm not buying that this is a good matchup. We know who the Texans are when they are right. I expect Tate to bounce back. Don't drop himMinnesota 23 – New Orleans 13WINNER: Kyler Murray, QB, VikingsFinally, we see a game with Kyler Murray and Justin Jefferson, and it's Murray's best game of the season. Keep in mind, he didn't have Jordan Addison, and T.J. Hockenson left almost immediately with a concussion. Murray ran for 51 yards. He could definitely be a streamer going forward.
FLUSH IT AND FORGET IT: The SaintsIt was the Vikings. Next week, they get the Giants. All will be forgotten.New York Jets 17 – Cleveland 12LOSER: The weatherCan we get a Sunday in New York/New Jersey with good weather? Some of us would like to go outside.POTENTIAL LOSER? Breece Hall, RB, Jets Braelon Allen was awesome in this game. Is he carving out a bigger role for when Breece Hall returns? I'm not convinced yet, but another good game next week at New England would make me nervous if I had Hall.

title: Packers vs. Bears: Jordan Love makes history, erupts in dominant win behind retooled offensive line - CBS Sports
description: Love's 367 yards passing are the most by a Packers QB vs. the Bears at Lambeau Field in series history
body:
Love's 367 yards passing are the most by a Packers QB vs. the Bears at Lambeau Field in series history
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:32 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Chicago Bears (3-2) entered Lambeau Field in Week 5 looking to honor their recently deceased former Hall of Fame player and head coach, Mike Ditka, against their archrival, the Green Bay Packers (3-2) on Sunday. Sunday's matchup between the NFC North foes went a lot like it did in the Brett Favre and Aaron Rodgers eras (1992-2022, 48-15 Packers, including the playoffs) than it did in Ditka's era as head coach (1982-1992, 15-5 Bears), with the Packers winning 31-7 behind a laser show from quarterback Jordan Love. Love completed 25 of his 31 throws for 367 yards and 2 touchdowns against Chicago, which makes him the Packers' record holder for the most passing yards in a game against the Bears at Lambeau Field. He beat the previous record of 345 yards passing by Lynn Dickey, set back in 1983. The victory, 24 points, ranks as the largest win against the Bears since 2014, the year Rodgers won the second of his four NFL MVPs. The Packers are now 5-3 against the Bears' in Love's eight career starts against them since 2023, including playoffs. "We were flowing today. Executed at a really high level. I was proud of everybody. That's what it looks like when we play to our standard, and we got playmakers making plays down the field, O-line doing a great job," Love said postgame on FOX. "That's the standard for us. ... This is huge. This is a win we needed at home, getting us rolling and keep building off this."Most pass yards by Packers QB vs. Bears at Lambeau Field, since 1957, when the stadium openedPass yardsSeasonJordan Love3672026Lynn Dickey3451983Aaron Rodgers3412021Brett Favre3361995Love went big-game hunting with regularity to both wide receiver Christian Watson (143 yards receiving and 2 receiving touchdowns on 6 catches) and wide receiver Matthew Golden (123 yards receiving on 6 catches), making Watson and Golden the first Green Bay duo with 120-plus yards receiving in a game since 2016. It last occurred when Davante Adams and Jordy Nelson accomplished the feat against the Tennessee Titans 10 years ago. Love hit Watson for gains of 42 yards (the game's first touchdown that made the score 7-0), 31 yards and 53 yards (Love's second touchdown pass that made the score 20-7 with 13:10 left in the third quarter). He connected with Golden on throws of 36 yards and 50 yards.In total, Love connected on six of eight of his eight throws of 20-plus air yards for a career-high 258 yards and 2 touchdowns on his passes of 20-plus air yards. Per the league's Next Gen stats, only Russell Wilson (264 with the New York Giants in Week 2 of the 2025 season against the Dallas Cowboys) had more in the NGS era (since 2016). According to ESPN Insights, Love joined Ben Roethlisberger as the only players with five completions of 30-plus air yards in a game since ESPN began tracking the metric 20 years ago in 2006. 

                                                                    Per the NFL's Next Gen Stats
                                                            Much of the credit for Love's game ought to go toward Green Bay's reworked offensive line. The Packers overhauled their offensive line with the signing of three veterans entering Week 4 in the aftermath of their 35-14 blowout home defeat on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 3 against the Atlanta Falcons: guard Laken Tomlinson, guard Kevin Zeitler and guard/tackle Mekhi Becton. Love had a season-high 2.76 average time to throw on Sunday against the Bears, and in each of the last two weeks at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (13.3% pressured rate) and against Chicago (23.5% pressured rate), he registered his two lowest pressured rates of the season. Not so coincidentally, Green Bay used the same offensive line starting five combination in each of the last two weeks: Jordan Morgan (left tackle), Tomlinson (left guard), Sean Rhyan (center), Travis Glover (right guard) and Anthony Belton (right tackle). Zeitler, a 36-year-old Pro Bowl guard, was active for the first time in Week 5, but he didn't register any offensive snaps in Week 5. He did contribute six snaps on special teams. Dominant defenseAfter the Bears were able to mount fourth-quarter comebacks with quarterback Caleb Williams in each of the last two meetings against the Packers, Chicago had nearly no offensive success against the Packers, averaging just 3.6 yards per play on Sunday, the lowest in a game for Bears head coach Ben Johnson in his career as an offensive coordinator and a head coach, which spans 73 games. They also tied their worst turnover margin (-5, five turnovers to zero takeaways) in a game since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger, per CBS Sports Research. Both Bears quarterbacks to enter the game, Tyson Bargent (87 yards passing and two interceptions on 12 of 21 throws) and Case Keenum (108 yards passing and an interception on 11 of 19 passing) threw interceptions, and Keenum also lost a fumble. Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze fumbling the football on a fourth-down completion accounted for the fifth giveaway. "They were flying around today," Love said of his defense. "I don't even know how many turnovers they had, but it felt like four. They were flying around, making plays left and right. Getting us the ball back, and they have been doing that all season, so like we said, we got some losses, but ... guys just making plays."
With a rebuilt offensive line providing Love much more time to throw and a ball-hawking defense, the Packers' defense's nine takeaways are the fourth most in the NFL entering the Week 5 late afternoon games. Green Bay can envision being a playoff contender once again. On the flip side, the Bears definitely need Williams, who is out with a hamstring injury, back in the lineup. Williams' return may not be able to fix Chicago's leaky secondary on the other side of the ball.

title: Raiders' Fernando Mendoza makes NFL debut: A look at how No. 1 overall pick performed - CBS Sports
description: The Raiders rookie QB was solid out of the gate in the Raiders' blowout loss
body:
The Raiders rookie QB was solid out of the gate in the Raiders' blowout loss
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:42 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It took until Week 5, but the 2026 No. 1 overall pick got to make his NFL debut. Down 45-17 in the fourth quarter against the New England Patriots, the Las Vegas Raiders opted to put Fernando Mendoza in to replace Kirk Cousins, marking the rookie's first appearance in the regular season. Mendoza took over for Cousins, who went 19-of-28 for 243 yards and one touchdown, with just over six minutes remaining. The 2025 Heisman Trophy winner had a solid start, starting off 5-for-5, including a 16-yard pass on Vegas' final drive of the game.The 23-year-old threw his first incompletion on 1st-and-10 on the Patriots' 20-yard line, followed by a 6-yard pass that set up 3rd-and-4 on the New England 14-yard line. An incomplete pass set up fourth down, and with nothing to lose, the Raiders went for it.Mendoza scrambled and had a decent run, but fell just short of the line to gain, prompting a turnover on downs and an eventual victory formation for the Patriots. The No. 1 overall pick's final stat line was 6-of-8 for 48 yards, with no touchdowns, picks or sacks taken.
Mendoza began the season as Cousins' backup and became the first No. 1 overall selected quarterback to not start Week 1 since 2018 (Baker Mayfield).Heading into this week, Cousins was tied for the league high in passing touchdowns with 11.The Patriots extended their win streak to two games and improved to 3-2 with the 45-17 win. The Raiders, who were one of the league's last remaining undefeated teams, are now 3-2, dropping their last two wins. Both teams have faced difficult AFC opponents the last two weeks, with the Patriots defeating the Buffalo Bills in Week 4 and the Raiders falling to the Kansas City Chiefs last week.
The Raiders have another challenge next week, when they face the Bills.

title: Marvin Harrison Jr. trade grades: Cardinals extract near-max value from Texans for former top-5 pick WR - CBS Sports
description: Arizona dealt Harrison Jr. for multiple draft picks, including a 2027 second-round pick
body:
Arizona dealt Harrison Jr. for multiple draft picks, including a 2027 second-round pick
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:37 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The awkward separation between wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. and the Arizona Cardinals is now complete. He is now a Houston Texan after his new team reportedly sent multiple draft picks to Arizona in exchange for the fourth overall pick from the 2024 NFL Draft. Houston shipped a 2027 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Cardinals in exchange for the 24-year-old wideout and a 2027 seventh-round draft choice. Harrison Jr., the son of Pro Football Hall of Famer Marvin Harrison, is now the first wide receiver since Ahmad Rashad in 1974 to be traded within his first three years in the NFL after being selected as a top-five pick, per CBS Sports Research. Rashad was also traded from the Cardinals and was shipped to the Buffalo Bills in exchange for quarterback Dennis Shaw.   WRs traded within first three seasons as top-five picks in Common Draft era (Since 1967)19742026Wide receiverAhmad RashadMarvin Harrison Jr.Overall pick4th4thTraded fromCardinalsCardinalsTraded toBuffalo BillsHouston TexansTrade compensation receivedQB Dennis Shaw2027 2nd-round pick, 2027 6th-round pickSo, who came out with the better haul in the exchange? Here are trade grades for both the Texans and the Cardinals in terms of how they made out in the deal. Houston Texans: C-The Houston Texans are grasping at straws in 2026. They are 1-4 and enter the late afternoon games in Week 5, averaging the second-fewest rushing yards per game (57.4) and the fewest rushing yards per carry (3.0) by a team's running back group in the entire league. Houston's disappointing start has nothing to do with quarterback C.J. Stroud. His 280.4 passing yards per game rank as the fourth-most in the NFL entering the Week 5 late afternoon games, and his 6-0 touchdown-to-interception ratio is tied for the second-best in the league. Stroud's 185 throws without an interception are now the fourth most in the league through four games in NFL history, per CBS Sports Research. That's why the Texans have made their second wide receiver trade of 2026 after dealing safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh-round pick to the New England Patriots this offseason in exchange for veteran wide receiver Kayshon Boutte. Stroud will be asked to put the Texans' offense on his back this season, so why not trade for a former collegiate target of his? He and Harrison Jr. were Ohio State teammates for two seasons from 2021 to 2022, and Harrison Jr.'s 14 receiving touchdowns when Stroud was the starting quarterback in 2022 are tied for the third most in a single season in Buckeyes' history.  Harrison Jr. also set or tied career-highs in catches (77), receiving yards (1,263) and receiving touchdowns (14) in that 2022 season with Stroud. Houston also needed another wide receiver to make an impact outside of two-time Pro Bowler Nico Collins, since once-exciting wide receiver Tank Dell's NFL career was sidetracked by a significant knee injury.  Dell went down in Week 16 of the 2024 season with a dislocated kneecap, torn ACL, LCL, MCL, and meniscus damage, and he hasn't played a game since. Most receiving TD in a season, Ohio State historyReceiving TDTerry Glenn (1995)17Jeremiah Smith (2024)15Marvin Harrison Jr. (2023)14Marvin Harrison Jr. (2022)*14*David Boston (1997)14* C.J. Stroud was Ohio State's starting QB in 2022Houston was desperate and filled a need, but what it spent to acquire Harrison is a little rich, given the writing was on the wall that Harrison Jr.'s Cardinals' career was coming to an end. Arizona Cardinals: B+The Cardinals did about as good a job as they could to recoup value for Harrison Jr., with everyone and their grandma aware that Harrison Jr.'s time in Arizona was a bust and about to end. A second-round pick in the vaunted 2027 NFL Draft is ideal. Plus, they moved up a round at the back of the draft, sending a 2027 seventh-round pick along with Harrison Jr. and getting a 2027 sixth-round pick back.Despite racking up 202 targets in Arizona, the third-most on the team since 2024, he totaled just 108 catches for 1,578 yards receiving and 13 receiving touchdowns while failing to build a consistent rapport with both Kyler Murray and Jacoby Brissett. He trailed only McBridge (362) and Wilson (241) in targets on the Cardinals since entering the league.Arizona could have earned an A- or an A if it had gotten a first-round pick in return for the former top-five pick. Harrison Jr. is under team contract for up to a maximum of three more seasons on his rookie deal, including the rest of 2026. That's a decent value for a team that believes all he needed was a change of scenery. However, what the Cardinals did receive back was solid, all things considered.

title: Seattle vs. San Francisco: 49ers' Dre Greenlaw ejected after head-butting Seahawks' Ernest Jones - CBS Sports
description: A late hit on Sam Darnold along the Seattle sideline spark
body:
A late hit on Sam Darnold along the Seattle sideline sparked a confrontation that ended with the San Francisco linebacker head-butting a helmetless player
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:13 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        Seattle Seahawks vs. San Francisco 49ers has been one of the best rivalries the NFL has had to offer in recent years, but things went a bit too far during the second quarter of their Week 5 matchup.49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw drew a flag for a late hit on Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold along the Seattle sideline. He was then confronted by several Seahawks players, including linebacker Ernest Jones. During the confrontation, Greenlaw head-butted the helmetless Jones, which led to his ejection. Check out what happened here:
Greenlaw is one of the 49ers' best players on defense, and entered this matchup ranked second on the team in tackles with 34. He's also their emotional leader. That was on full display during San Francisco's Week 4 victory against the Denver Broncos last Sunday, when he confronted his former head coach Sean Payton, telling him to "Get the f--k off the field." He was also fined $11,941 by the league for taunting the Broncos' bench. "He was fired up all week," George Kittle said of Greenlaw last Sunday. "I think you could've asked anybody who played with Dre Greenlaw for his first four or five years he was here, I think 90% of the roster would say that he was their favorite teammate."
As evidenced by Sunday, sometimes that emotion can have unwanted ramifications. Greenlaw received a one-game suspension last season when he ran after an official and jawed at them following a game-winning field goal. Officials have also ejected him twice in previous games. Greenlaw was kicked out of a game in 2022 following a helmet-to-helmet hit on Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert, and then during the 2022 playoffs, when he famously got into an altercation with Philadelphia Eagles head of security Dom DiSandro.

title: Kentucky fined $500K by SEC after fans storm field to celebrate wild overtime win vs. Lane Kiffin's LSU squad - CBS Sports
description: The Wildcats were fined for violation of the leagues's access to competition area policy
body:
The Wildcats were fined for violation of the leagues's access to competition area policy
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:34 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Kentucky's successful two-point conversion in overtime to beat LSU 35-34 on Saturday night was a costly one after thousands of students poured onto Kroger Field celebrating the program's epic victory.The SEC has fined the Wildcats $500,000 — which is owed directly to LSU — for violating the league's access to competition area policy after fans stormed the field.It's a not-so-small price to pay for Kentucky's first home victory over a top-10 team since the 2021 season and marks first-year coach Will Stein's second such win of the campaign.The Wildcats surged from unranked to No. 15 in Sunday's Week 7 AP Poll as a result.
The SEC's policy states that "institutions shall limit access to competition areas to participating student-athletes, coaches, officials, support personnel and properly credentialed or authorized individuals at all times.  For the safety of participants and spectators alike, at no time before, during or after a contest may spectators enter the competition area."
        
            
                LSU's road woes continue as Kentucky stuns No. 10 Tigers, adding pressure to CFP hopes
                
                    Austin Nivison                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Moments after Kentucky kicker Adam Zouagui forced overtime in the final minute of regulation, the Wildcats opted to go for the win on a successful two-point conversion for the second consecutive game. Quarterback Kenny Minchey ran through the middle of LSU's defensive front untouched in the Wildcats' four-wide look for the victory.Zouagui had previously missed two chip-shot field goals in the fourth quarter before forcing the extra session with 1:30 left in the contest.
"That's the life of a kicker," Stein said in his post-game press conference. "You've got everybody watching you on those kicks. It was unfortunate that he missed two, but he hit a really big one. We do pressure kicks all the time in practice. I've seen him hit it a million times. He did a great job in that moment."The league eliminated its escalating fines policy ahead of the 2025 season in favor of a more direct, costly punishment for field storming situations."The motivation was 'field rushing is field rushing, the first time or the 18th time,'" SEC commissioner Greg Sankey said last spring. "The random nature of, if you're the one getting rushed, it doesn't feel good. It might be the first time (it happened) there, but it might be your sixth time in a row, literally."
Under the previous system, SEC schools were fined $100,000 for the first offense, $250,000 for the second offense and $500,000 for any violations of the rule thereafter. The SEC also now has the authority to waive a fine if the visiting team and game officials are allowed to return safely to their respective locker rooms before fans enter the playing area. According to the league office, the SEC's access to competition area policy "allows for member institutions to adopt an institutional policy that permits fans to celebrate on the playing surface once all visiting team personnel and game officials have safely exited the field or court.  The school must submit the plan to the Conference office in advance and communicate the policy to fans. If all visiting team personnel and game officials are safely off the playing surface prior to fans entering the field or court, then the home institution may avoid the prescribed penalty."

title: Week 5 Fantasy Football standouts: Week 6 early waiver wire adds - CBS Sports
description: Drake Maye and Christian Watson delivered explosive multi-touchdown performances to lead this week's biggest rise
body:
Drake Maye and Christian Watson delivered explosive multi-touchdown performances to lead this week's biggest risers, while two Patriots wideouts highlight early targets on the waiver wire
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:18 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        After a slow start to the early slate games, Week 5 of the Fantasy Football season kicked into a higher gear with more touchdowns in the witching hour of the early slate and the late games. As we move forward to Week 6, it's important to note several players who stood out in Week 5 and others who should be at the top of your priority waiver wire add list. But first, let's look at some players whose stock has risen in Week 5. These players are back on track to be weekly winners and must-start players, and may also find themselves featured on playoff and championship-winning rosters.Drake Maye, QB, PatriotsIf you bought low on Maye, congratulations. Not only is he running again, but he's also finding his way as a passer by leaning on the vertical shot plays that made him an MVP candidate in 2025. Maye has adjusted better to his offensive line injuries than any other quarterback dealing with a similar slew in 2026. After a massive Week 4 performance, Maye put even more Fantasy points on the board in Week 5 with 374 yards passing, four passing touchdowns, and 25 yards rushing (plus another rushing score). He won you your week.Mike Evans, WR, 49ersIt was a slow start to the 49ers debut for Evans as he dealt with multiple injuries. Even now, he is playing through two broken ribs, but that can't slow down the Hall of Fame wide receiver who is a perfect fit for Brock Purdy's style. Evans looked unguardable in Week 5 against a top-tier Seahawks defense. He racked up 113 yards on seven receptions with a touchdown and nearly scored a second touchdown. He also saw double-digit targets, and it was no surprise that the 49ers' offense woke up once they started designing the offense around him. Isaiah Likely, TE, GiantsLikely continues to prove himself as one of the most impactful free agent signings by any team in 2026. He was targeted a whopping 13 times and turned those into 11 receptions for 94 yards and two touchdowns. Likely is a clear-cut top-six tight end and weekly must-start player in all formats. 
Christian Watson, WR, PackersWhen Watson returned from injury last season, we saw a brand new role for him. He was finally being featured all over the field and formation, in different roles, and no longer being asked to just win as a vertical receiver. However, that doesn't mean he forgot how to do that. He's still one of the best in the NFL at winning on the vertical plane, and with years of rapport built in with Jordan Love, we saw what that could mean in Week 5. Watson racked up eight targets, 143 receiving yards, six catches and two touchdowns. He continues to be one of the breakout top-10 WR buys of the 2026 Fantasy season and a likely league winner.Early Week 6 Waiver Wire TargetsDemario Douglas, WR, PatriotsAll tides rise with the Patriots offense if Drake Maye is back to playing MVP football again. We'll see if that stands, but if it does, you'll want to add Douglas now. In a season where consistent wide receivers are exceedingly difficult to find in Fantasy, Douglas' role is an interesting one. He makes important catches and uncovers in the red zone and tight confined areas. In Week 5, that meant two touchdowns and a top-12 finish.Kyle Williams, WR, PatriotsOn Beyond the Boxscore, Jacob and I haven't stopped mentioning how great Kyle Williams' All-22 film is. That has been the case since we saw his tape at Washington State and dates back to his rookie season in New England. All he does is make plays when given the opportunity. He caught three for 91 yards and an impressive quick-win vertical touchdown in Week 5. The issue is opportunity. He hasn't gotten much of it. Maybe this is a wake up call that he needs to.
Darius Cooper, WR, EaglesCooper continues to make big plays for an Eagles offense desperate for a spark without Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith. Cooper had a long touchdown on a beautiful connection with Jalen Hurts in Week 5. He finished with 71 yards and a touchdown on two receptions. He's a better add in non-PPR formats.Samaje Perine, RB, BengalsDon't look now, but this isn't the workhorse role managers who drafted him had hoped for with Chase Brown. Perine had a whopping 14 carries in Week 5. He turned those into 68 yards, but more importantly, he was used in the red zone and scored a touchdown reception with two catches on two targets for 10 yards. Perine is worth adding in all leagues. Jaylin Noel, WR, TexansThe Marvin Harrison Jr. trade clouds Noel's outlook, but the second-year wide receiver showed he was capable of getting over the top of coverage once again in Week 5. Noel scored a touchdown and caught a season-high five receptions. The talent is there and he's a nice deep-league stash given Nico Collins' injury.

title: Week 5 overreactions: Vikings as Super Bowl contenders, NFC East, Dan Quinn, and other thoughts - CBS Sports
description: The Minnesota Vikings have the longest active winning streak in the NFL.Yes, those Minnesota Vikings, who just made the Saints the lates
body:
The Minnesota Vikings have the longest active winning streak in the NFL.Yes, those Minnesota Vikings, who just made the Saints the latest victim of the Brian Flores torture chamber defense. This is a team that's now won 10 straight games dating back to last year. In Flores' latest masterpiece, the Vikings held Tyler Shough to 96 passing yards, no touchdowns and two interceptions. Minnesota basically doubled New Orleans in time of possession and owned a 364-142 yardage advantage.In this column, I try not to get overboard too quickly — it's still early, yada yada — but it's time to really project forward, and the Vikings might be the least-talked-about 5-0 team in NFL history.So let's talk about them.The Vikings are legit Super Bowl contendersOverreaction or reality: RealitySome numbers lie. These don't:The Vikings lead the NFL in defensive success rate (66.5%). That would be the best number in the past decade.The Vikings lead the NFL in defensive EPA per play (0.22). That would be the second-best number in the past decade.The Vikings lead the NFL in sack rate (9.8%). That would be the fifth-best number in the past decade.And that sack rate isn't a fluke. They had the fourth-best sack rate of the past decade last year.Flores is the best coordinator in the NFL. We already knew this defense was excellent, but it was encouraging to see Kyler Murray play his best game with the Vikings yet. He completed 24 of 30 passes (80%) for 229 yards and a touchdown to Justin Jefferson, and he ran the ball seven times for another 54 yards, excluding three kneeldowns. They aren't absurdly good numbers, but they don't need to be if the defense is going to be this dominant.Here's the stuff Murray can do to take this team to another level. The Vikings were actually down 7-6 early in the third quarter before a touchdown drive where Murray scrambled for 18 yards on third-and-10 and then threw a beauty of a touchdown to Jefferson on third-and-6.
Later, with the score tied, Murray sparked what proved to be the game-winning drive with a 32-yard pass to Jeshaun Jones. This was by far his best performance in Minnesota, and it makes sense considering he suffered a concussion in Week 1. The Vikings' ground game also had its best day, a byproduct of not only Murray's running but the threat of his running.Murray doesn't have to be great. But if he can take care of the ball, find Jefferson — who made some spectacular catches — and make a few timely plays, this is a legitimate Super Bowl contender.Texans can still make the playoffsOverreaction or reality: RealityOnly one team — the 1992 Chargers — has made the playoffs after starting 0-4. Can the 2026 Texans join them? It shouldn't be ruled out.
The Texans thumped the hapless Titans 26-3. With DeMeco Ryans taking over play-calling, the defense was at its very best, allowing just 187 yards and 3.2 yards per play. Will Anderson Jr., who is on track to not only win Defensive Player of the Year but potentially dominate the vote, sacked Cam Ward three times, and Houston forced two turnovers. C.J. Stroud threw for one touchdown and ran for another.But this isn't really about this game, because the Titans are hardly a good measuring stick. Rather, it's about what the Texans still can do. Remember, this is an organization that made the playoffs after starting 0-3 last year. This year's team isn't last year's team, but it can have similar success, especially because Stroud is playing really well when Nico Collins is on the field. Plus, look at the Texans' upcoming schedule:Week 6: vs. Jaguars in LondonWeek 7: vs. GiantsWeek 8: BYEWeek 9: at ChargersWeek 10: at BrownsWeek 11: vs. ColtsThe Texans could be favored in all of those games, or at least the next five after the Jaguars game. If the defense is back to dominating, writing off the Texans simply because history says 0-4 teams don't make the postseason would be a mistake.
The NFC East winner will have a losing recordOverreaction or reality: OverreactionThe NFC East did not have a banner week. The Cowboys dropped a home game to the previously winless Buccaneers, led by undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, on Thursday. Sunday morning, the Eagles lost after taking a two-point lead with eight seconds and inexplicably giving the Jaguars a returnable kickoff. After a big return, Cam Little made a 57-yard field goal as time expired, and Nick Sirianni said, "I cost us that game."All of that paled in comparison to the utter disaster that was the end of the Commanders-Giants game. With no timeouts left and well within field goal range, Washington somehow ran out of time with a completely incompetent final sequence.
That means the 3-1-1 Giants are still in first place in the division, the Cowboys and Eagles are 2-3, and the Commanders are 1-3-1 and reeling.
It becomes really, really difficult to see any team in this division reaching 10 wins, simply because each team has major issues. The Cowboys can't defend anyone. The Eagles can't score. The Giants are putting their trust in Jameis Winston, and the Commanders can't stop anyone and seem on the brink of collapsing completely.Only once has the NFC East (as currently constructed) had a champion with a losing record. I won't go that far yet, but no team reaching double-digit wins is very much on the table.The Commanders should fire Dan Quinn ... but they probably can't right nowOverreaction or reality: RealityI hate advocating for anyone to be fired, but the NFL is a results-driven business, and the results just aren't good enough for the Commanders. As Quinn said, Sunday's tie feels like a loss, and it feels like another lost season in the nation's capital.
And that's a bummer, because Jayden Daniels looked truly excellent in his return from a dislocated elbow. The chance for the Commanders to be right in the thick of things in such an underwhelming division was right there.Quinn put all the blame for the debacle on his shoulders, as he should have. But the idea that it's time for him to be fired goes deeper than Sunday. A week earlier, a poor fourth-and-1 decision using a third-string quarterback turned a winnable game against the Colts into a blowout loss. Sunday, he made another poor fourth-down decision, opting to punt from positive territory instead of going for it. The Giants' offense was rolling with three touchdowns on three drives to force overtime, and then in overtime, New York had moved the ball again easily but missed a field goal.Giving the Giants a possession in a next-score-win scenario, therefore, was a bad idea. Cam Skattebo actually bailed Quinn out with a horrible fumble with the Giants again in field goal range, only for Quinn to make his worst mistake yet. Washington has now won just three of its past 17 games.
Quinn's performance has been fire-worthy. The thing is, the Commanders have two first-time coordinators. There is one former head coach on staff — running backs coach Anthony Lynn — but upending the staff would be a tough development in a season that's quickly slipping from returning to the playoffs to simply hoping Daniels can stay healthy and continue to progress. Owner Josh Harris is known for being patient (he owns the "Trust the Process" 76ers), and, in his first year as Washington's owner, he gave Ron Rivera an entire season.Long story short, Quinn will likely keep his job at least through the end of the year, but that is more a product of circumstance than of deserving it.The Dolphins need to bench Malik WillisOverreaction or reality: OverreactionMalik Willis was in the news this week when Bengals safety Jordan Battle told reporters he had a "tell" for when Willis would throw. And guess who picked off Willis twice Sunday? Jordan Battle.
I won't sit here and say Willis was good Sunday. His second interception was awful. He was once again very inaccurate, and he has the highest off-target rate in the NFL this season by far.But there are three reasons the Dolphins shouldn't bench Willis:They owe it to themselves to see this through. This was always going to be a really rough season, but they signed Willis to a three-year deal as a sort of in-between attempt at a solution. If Willis played well, he would be a cheap solution at the game's most important position. If he doesn't, he can easily be replaced after the season. It's worth at least trying.The passing numbers are ugly, but because Willis is such an effective runner, he was actually OK on Sunday. His -0.02 EPA per dropback is slightly below average, but nothing awful. The Dolphins rolled up 217 yards and two touchdowns on the ground. Their most effective path to being in games is pounding the run and hoping to get some turnover luck. Willis is a huge part of the running game (he had 74 rushing yards and a score on Sunday).Most importantly, if it's not Malik Willis, who's it going to be? Kyle McCord, who has never played in an NFL game, is the only other quarterback on the roster. Willis is a captain. The offense is designed around his mobility. For such a young team, the Dolphins demoting him would be a bad move.Turnovers will doom the SeahawksOverreaction or reality: OverreactionA big part of the Seahawks giving up 32 points was four(!) turnovers, including an absolutely inexcusable George Holani fumble just seconds before halftime that resulted in a 49ers touchdown.The Seahawks now have nine turnovers this season; entering "Sunday Night Football," only four teams have more. Sam Darnold has always been turnover-prone, and he had two picks Sunday.
But what if I told you the Seahawks had 28 turnovers last year, second-most in the NFL? Surely, you can't win a Super Bowl like that, right? Wrong, apparently. After all those regular-season turnovers, Seattle had zero turnovers in the postseason.The turnovers are an issue right now -- don't get me wrong -- and they could continue to be an issue. Especially for Darnold, they tend to pop up in bunches. Even so, this is a team built to win double-digit games, and once you get to the postseason, anything can happen, as we saw with this team last year.Trey McBride and Ja'Marr Chase both made legit 'Catch of the Year' candidatesOverreaction or reality: RealityIt kind of feels like a "If it happened in a game featuring the Cardinals or Dolphins, did it really happen?" season. Arizona and Miami seem very much out of the national consciousness, and I get it. But if you missed these ridiculous catch ... let me do you a favor:
Absolutely absurd.

title: Bengals' Jordan Battle intercepts Malik Willis twice after finding tell in Miami QB's throwing mechanics - CBS Sports
description: Battle's huge second quarter in Week 5 may have been no coincidence
body:
Battle's huge second quarter in Week 5 may have been no coincidence
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:54 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Cincinnati Bengals' defense should take a collective bow after identifying and exploiting an advantage over the Miami Dolphins in Week 5.Prior to the game, safety Jordan Battle revealed that the Bengals noticed a subtle tell in Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis' throwing mechanics that they felt they could use to time their pass defense. They seemingly did just that when battle intercepted Willis twice in the first half of their meeting on Sunday."He has a slight little tap before every throw, so I feel like we could use that as a key to break on the ball," Battle said after the Bengals' Thursday practice. "He likes to tap the ball before he throws it, or he takes his hand off, and that gives the read to break."How much of a role the tell played in Battle's two takeaways is uncertain. Perhaps it was a coincidence that he was the one to both point it out publicly and haul in a pair of interceptions, or maybe he and his teammates were in the right place at the right time after spotting it.
The first interception was primarily a product of the pass rush, not Battle's position group in the secondary. Boye Mafe pressured Willis and got his hand on the ball during the release, which shortened its trajectory and made it playable for Battle.
Five minutes later, Battle made an excellent play on the ball for his second pick of the second quarter. As Willis rolled out of the pocket, Battle left his assignment to step in front of the intended receiver and beat him to the ball.If Willis' tell impacted either play, it is more likely that it did so on this one than the first.
At the time of Willis' second interception, he had more passes caught by Cincinnati defenders than Miami receivers. He was 1-for-7 for 22 yards late in the second quarter. The Bengals capitalized on the second takeaway with a touchdown on the ensuing possession to take a 21-7 lead into the locker room at halftime.Revealing the tell before the game was a risky move for Battle. If Willis and the Dolphins were not already keen on the tendency, they certainly were after Battle's media availability. They may have already discovered it through self-scouting, but if not, three days was not much time to eliminate the habit from Willis' mechanics.Cincinnati entered the week with a bottom-tier pass defense, so any advantages it could identify would be welcome. The Bengals ranked in the bottom half of the league in EPA per pass, interceptions, time to throw, pass yards per game and average yards of separation. Sunday's performance should deliver a climb in the statistical rankings.

title: Marvin Harrison Jr. trade: Cardinals send former top-5 pick to Texans for multiple draft choices - CBS Sports
description: Harrison Jr. reunites with his Ohio State quarterback C.J. Stroud in Houston after a failure to launch in Arizona
body:
Harrison Jr. reunites with his Ohio State quarterback C.J. Stroud in Houston after a failure to launch in Arizona
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:16 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Arizona Cardinals' divorce with 2024 fourth overall pick wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. is actually happening. Arizona is trading the 24-year-old, along with a 2027 seventh-round pick, to the Houston Texans for a 2027 second-round draft pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick, according to ESPN. Texans head coach confirmed the trade on Sunday, following Houston's first win of the year, a 26-3 victory over the Tennessee Titans.The trade was announced during the Cardinals' game against the Detroit Lions, a game in which Harrison was inactive due to the pending trade. Rumors swirled over the weekend that a trade could be imminent, and now Harrison will get a fresh start after his time with the Cardinals didn't go as expected. Texans quarterback and Harrison's former Ohio State teammate C.J. Stroud was asked about the trade after his game. "You want to know more? I don't know what more I can tell you," Stroud said with a smile. "I think he's a great guy, think he's a great player, and I'm excited to get him here."
The Texans were one of the top teams in the conversations surrounding a Harrison trade, in large part due to the wide receiver's connection with Stroud. The two played at Ohio State together in 2021 and 2022. On Saturday, as the trade rumors were taking over the league, CBS Sports' Aditi Kinkhabwala spoke with Stroud about Harrison."[Stroud] told me [Harrison's] an amazing talent, he told me he's a great teammate, he said that he still believes in what he can do. And he also said he's one of the hardest workers he's ever known ... Stroud said sometimes a fresh start can be really good," Kinkhabwala said.If Stroud and Harrison can replicate, or even come close to replicating, what they did together at Ohio State, the Texans' offense will see a dramatic improvement. Harrison set or tied career-highs in receptions (77), receiving yards (1,263) and receiving touchdowns (14) in 2022 at Ohio State with Stroud at the helm.
Harrison Jr. struggled to stand out for the 1-3 Cardinals early in 2026 with five catches for 85 yards receiving and a touchdown. His five catches are tied for sixth on Arizona, ranking behind All-Pro tight end Trey McBride (33), wide receiver Michael Wilson (25), wide receiver Kendrick Bourne (13), rookie running back Jeremiyah Love (11) and running back Tyler Allgeier (10). For his Cardinals career, he totaled 108 catches for 1,578 yards receiving and 13 receiving touchdowns despite 202 targets, the third-most on the team since 2024. He trailed only McBridge (362) and Wilson (241) in targets in the span of his young career. The Texans need another wide receiver to emerge for Stroud, aside from two-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Nico Collins, with once-promising wide receiver Tank Dell's career derailed by injury. Dell went down in Week 16 of the 2024 season with a dislocated kneecap, torn ACL, LCL, MCL, and meniscus damage, and he hasn't suited up since. Harrison Jr., the son of Pro Football Hall of Famer Marvin Harrison, is now the first wide receiver since Ahmad Rashad in 1974 to be traded within his first three NFL seasons after being selected in the top five of the NFL draft, per CBS Sports Research. Rashad was also traded from the Cardinals and was sent to the Buffalo Bills in exchange for quarterback Dennis Shaw. 
Harrison is also now the fifth top-5 pick to be traded before year four in the past 10 years. The others in the same category are quarterback Zach Wilson (traded from the New York Jets to the Denver Broncos in 2024), quarterback Trey Lance (traded from the San Francisco 49ers to the Dallas Cowboys in 2023), cornerback Jeff Okudah (traded from the Detroit Lions to the Atlanta Falcons in 2023) and quarterback Sam Darnold (traded from the Jets to the Carolina Panthers in 2021).Defending Super Bowl champion Darnold is the only player on the list to see actual success in their career after their initial trade, though it did take many stops before he got there.

title: Aaron Rodgers passes Peyton Manning, Ben Roethlisberger in NFL record book after Week 5 win - CBS Sports
description: Rodgers' big day helped the Steelers improve to 3-2
body:
Rodgers' big day helped the Steelers improve to 3-2
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:32 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Sunday was an eventful day for Aaron Rodgers, whose farewell season is off to a 3-2 start for the Steelers following their win over the Colts. Not only did Pittsburgh secure a 34-22 win against Indianapolis, but Rodgers made some improvements in the NFL record books, passing both Hall of Fame quarterback Peyton Manning and former Steelers quarterback Ben Roethlisberger.Rodgers moved past Manning to No. 3 on the career touchdown pass list when he connected with Jaylen Warren on an 80-yard score in the first quarter. Rodgers and Manning had been tied at 579 touchdown passes prior to Sunday. After the win, Rodgers spoke to what it means to him to move past such a legendary quarterback on an all-time list.
"Anytime you're in the same sentence as Peyton [Manning], that definitely does mean a lot to me," Rodgers told CBS Sports' Tracy Wolfson, adding with a smile that he thinks he "earned that one" because he took a shot on the pass.
Manning, who played from 1998-15, is the only player who has more league MVPs than Rodgers. Manning won the award a record five times (2003, 2004, 2008, 2009, and 2013), while Rodgers has won it four times (2011, 2014, 2020, and 2021). Rodgers now trails only Tom Brady (737) and Drew Brees (608) in career touchdown passes. 
Rodgers also passed Roethlisberger with his 166th regular-season win as a starting NFL quarterback. He now has sole possession of fifth all-time in that department behind only Tom Brady (251), former teammate Brett Favre (186), Peyton Manning (186) and Drew Brees (172).  On Sunday, Rodgers had his best game of the season despite three of his receivers being out due to injury. Rodgers, who threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns on 22-of-31 passing, became the first Steelers quarterback since Hall of Famer Terry Bradshaw to throw three touchdowns in three consecutive games. Rodgers received big contributions on Sunday from Warren, tight end Pat Freiermuth, and rookie wideout Germie Bernard. Freiermuth caught two touchdown passes, and Bernard set a season-high with 80 yards on six receptions. 
Warren, who is enjoying his best season to date, ran for 101 yards on 15 carries and had 87 yards on six catches. He is the first player since Herschel Walker back in 1986 to have an 80-yard touchdown catch and a 50-yard touchdown run in the same game. 
Rodgers was well-protected by an offensive line that had been under some heat following last week's loss to Cleveland. The unit, which includes a relatively new starter in rookie first-round pick Max Iheanachor, allowed just one sack and helped Pittsburgh amass 112 yards on 16 carries. Defensively, the Steelers forced the Colts to settle for five field goals and came up with two turnovers on downs late in the game, as the Colts were attempting a comeback. It wasn't a dominant performance, but Pittsburgh's defense nonetheless showed signs of growth after its struggles in Cleveland 10 days ago. 
Linebacker Payton Wilson and defensive back Jalen Ramsey specifically stood out for the Steelers. Wilson had 10 tackles and a key pass breakup on fourth down. Ramsey had nine tackles despite playing with a broken wrist. He also had a perfectly-timed hit that prevented a big play in the first half. 
With the win, Pittsburgh is now 3-0 at home this season. It'll look to pick up its first road win of the season next Sunday against the Buccaneers, who won their first game of the season last Thursday night in Dallas.

schema.headline: Aaron Rodgers passes Peyton Manning, Ben Roethlisberger in NFL record book after Week 5 win - CBS Sports

title: Will the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade unlock his potential? History offers hope, and a warning - CBS Sports
description: The Arizona Cardinals felt they were getting their next star receiver when they drafted Marvin Harrison Jr. at No. 4 overall in the 2024
body:
The Arizona Cardinals felt they were getting their next star receiver when they drafted Marvin Harrison Jr. at No. 4 overall in the 2024 NFL Draft and now, less than three years later, the team is moving on. The Cardinals finalized a deal to trade the former Ohio State star to the Houston Texans.Harrison was told on Saturday that he would be inactive for Sunday's game against the Lions as the details of the trade were finalized. The Harrison experiment certainly didn't go the way either side expected, as 1,000-yard seasons seemed ahead of him and frequent trips to the end zone felt like a guarantee. When Harrison joined the league after such a successful run with the Buckeyes, it didn't take much imagination to envision what the two-time unanimous All-American's NFL career might look like and the future looked hopeful. Thirty-three games later, we're having a very different conversation: Will Harrison be better off playing somewhere other than Arizona?
Maybe. And soon we will find out. Trading for Harrison requires believing two things for the Texans: that the Cardinals haven't gotten the most out of him, and that another team can do better. The first argument is getting easier to make. The second is where things get complicated, especially when you look at what's happened to other highly drafted receivers who fell short of expectations early in their careers.The No. 4 pick comes with expectationsIn my recent story on Carnell Tate, the fourth pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, we looked at what teams should expect from receivers drafted in the top 10. The average rookie season over the last decade was 901 receiving yards. Harrison finished with 885 in 2024, a respectable start, even if it fell short of expectations.But things haven't gotten better. Harrison managed 608 yards in 12 games last season, and through four games in 2026, he has five catches for 85 yards. For perspective, Seahawks rookie running back Jadarian Price, who played three games before landing on IR, has four receptions. This is the same Price who was targeted just 14 times over his final two seasons at Notre Dame. Harrison was targeted at least 13 times in four different games during his final season at Ohio State.
So yeah.Through 33 NFL games, Harrison has 1,578 receiving yards. Amari Cooper, also drafted fourth overall, had 2,285 yards at the same point. Corey Davis, the fifth pick in 2017, had 1,503. Harrison's production looks much closer to Davis's than Cooper's.Harrison vs. first-round receivers early in their careersStatisticHarrison1st-round WR avg.Rank (53 WRs)Receiving yards/game47.853.033rdReceptions/game3.273.7335thReceiving TD/game0.390.3017thCatch rate53.5%59.3%46thYards/target7.818.2231stYards after catch/reception2.54.5T-51stExplosive catches/target20.8%18.4%9thThere are encouraging numbers here. Harrison's 13 touchdowns are more than Cooper (12) or CeeDee Lamb (11) had through their first 33 games. He's also ninth in explosive receptions per target. But he's near the bottom in catch rate and yards after the catch. The big plays are there; the consistent production isn't.Harrison was playing more, but producing lessPerhaps the biggest concern isn't simply that Harrison has struggled. It's that he became less involved in Arizona's offense, even while playing more.Among 41 first-round receivers in their first four appearances of Year 3, Harrison ranks 39th in receiving yards and is tied for the fewest receptions.Harrison's disappearing opportunitiesStatisticFirst 29 games2026 (4 games)Typical Year 3 1st-round WRReceiving yards/game51.521.364.8Targets/game6.53.37.5Catch rate54.5%38.5%60.9%Routes/game31.835.532.3Targets per route20.5%9.2%22.7%That last row tells the story. Harrison was targeted on roughly one of every five routes through his first 29 games. This season, it's fewer than one in 10. And that raises a fair question: Is Harrison struggling because he isn't getting opportunities, or is he not getting opportunities because he's struggling?There's evidence for both. Harrison ran 17 go routes in the first two games, tied for sixth most in the league, and Jacoby Brissett took some responsibility after Harrison went without a catch. But we can't blame everything on the quarterback or scheme when Trey McBride and Michael Wilson have combined for 58 receptions through four games. Harrison has five.Getting better isn't the same as becoming a starDespite the social-media noise, I'd be careful about giving up on Harrison. Plenty of first-round receivers have needed time to develop, but there's a difference between becoming productive and becoming the player a team thought it was drafting.Corey Davis, Mike Williams and DeVante Parker all improved after modest beginnings. Each had at least one season that justified some of that early optimism. The problem? None consistently produced like the elite receiver his draft position suggested. And Davis was drafted the highest of the three, at No. 5 overall, one spot after Harrison.Then there's Lamb, who went from a good young player to one of the NFL's best. But he was already averaging more than 62 yards per game through 33 appearances, considerably better than Harrison's 47.8.How other first-round WRs developedWR (draft pick)First 33 games YPGGames 34+ YPGNotable later seasonMarvin Harrison Jr. (4th)47.8TBDTBDCorey Davis (5th)45.555.9984 yards (2020)DeVante Parker (14th)44.748.71,202 (2019)Mike Williams (7th)35.751.41,146 (2021)Marquise Brown (25th)48.143.61,008 (2021)CeeDee Lamb (17th)62.690.41,749 (2023)Amari Cooper (4th)69.266.01,250 (2023)Williams and Parker eventually had 1,000-yard seasons, and Davis nearly got there with 984 in 2020. Harrison is young enough to make a similar leap. But Cooper and Lamb were already much more productive at this stage. That's an important distinction.What a trade can (and can't) fixSo what happens when a first-round receiver gets a fresh start somewhere else?Amari Cooper is the obvious success story. In 2018, Oakland traded him to Dallas, where his production jumped from 46.7 to 80.6 yards per game. He followed that with consecutive 1,000-yard seasons. Brandin Cooks also flourished after New England acquired him from New Orleans in 2017, producing 1,082 yards before adding 1,204 with the Rams the following year.But here's the difference: Both Cooper and Cooks had already posted two 1,000-yard seasons before being traded. Their new teams weren't betting on production they'd never seen. They were building on what those receivers had already done.The other historical comparisons aren't nearly as encouraging.I looked at first-round receivers traded in Year 3 or Year 4, the same stage of Harrison's career. Some joined better offenses or played with better quarterbacks. Most never became the players their new teams hoped they would.First-round WR trades in Years 3-4: Price and productionReceiverTraded from → toTrade returnBefore tradeAfter tradePhillip Dorsett (2017)Colts → PatriotsJacoby Brissett528 yards (2016)194 (2017)290 (2018)397 (2019)Corey Coleman (2018)Browns → Bills7th305 (2017)Released by BUF71 with NYG (2018)Jalen Reagor (2022)Eagles → Vikings7th + conditional 4th/5th299 (2021)104 (2022)138 (2023)100 (2024)Jahan Dotson (2024)Commanders → Eagles3rd + two 7ths; 5th sent with Dotson518 (2023)216 (2024)262 (2025)Brandin Cooks (2017)Saints → Patriots1st + 3rd; 4th sent with Cooks1,173 (2016)1,082 (2017)1,204 (2018)583 (2019)Sammy Watkins (2017)Bills → RamsE.J. Gaines + 2nd; 6th sent with Watkins430 in 8 games (2016)593 (2017)519 (2018)673 (2019)Kelvin Benjamin (2017)Panthers → Bills3rd + 7th475 in 8 CAR games217 in 6 BUF games380 (2018)Amari Cooper (2018)Raiders → Cowboys1st280 in 6 OAK games725 in 9 DAL games1,189 (2019)1,114 (2020)N'Keal Harry (2022)Patriots → Bears7th184 (2021)116 (2022)no rec (2023)Hollywood Brown (2022)Ravens → Cardinals1st; 3rd sent with Brown1,008 (2021)709 (2022)574 (2023)91 in 2g (2024)Cooper is the clearest example of a receiver taking his game to another level. Cooks maintained his production, while Sammy Watkins remained useful without ever returning to his 1,000-yard form.But Dorsett, Coleman, Reagor, Dotson and Harry? None became the player their original teams envisioned. Injuries played a role in some cases, but changing teams didn't solve the larger problem. And that's something Harrison's new team should keep in mind when setting their expectations. The price needs to reflect the gambleOf course, there's another reason Harrison is appealing: his contract. His new team will inherit his remaining 2026 salary and 2027 compensation, with the possibility to exercise his fifth-year option for 2028.But what should it cost to acquire him? Houston parted with a pair of 2027 draft picks, one in the second round and another in the sixth.The historical returns vary considerably. Dallas sent a first-rounder for Cooper. New England gave up a first and third for Cooks, getting a fourth back. Arizona surrendered a first for Hollywood Brown, with a third coming back. All three receivers had already proved themselves.Meanwhile, Dotson cost a third and two sevenths, with a fifth going the other way. Harry and Coleman each brought back seventh-round picks.Harrison falls somewhere in between. He wasn't going to fetch a first-rounder, but a third felt closer to his worth given his production and untapped potential. But remember, Pittsburgh got a 2028 second-round pick for Joey Porter Jr. when plenty of people thought a third was the best-case scenario.Put another way: You never know. If Houston believes it can unlock Harrison, a second-rounder might feel like a bargain. But at that price, whoever the mystery buyer is, better have a plan for using him.The gambleI think Harrison can be better than he's been in Arizona. We all saw what he did at Ohio State, and we've seen flashes of that ability in the NFL. The issue has been consistency.The tougher questions are how much better he can be, and what another team should give up to find out.Cooper showed that a change of scenery can work. But history also shows how often a fresh start changes very little, particularly for receivers who haven't already established themselves as consistently productive.

schema.headline: Will the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade unlock his potential? History offers hope, and a warning - CBS Sports
